resources.string: What is new in each version

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_16_bullets
string-array.item: Only the current timed line changes color and grows by 20% in the lyrics sheet, landscape lyrics and player card. Earlier and upcoming lines keep their normal appearance.
Unsynced lyrics and the time before the first line have no highlighted phrase. Stable line measurements avoid shifting the scroll target.

resources.string: More space in the landscape player

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_15_bullets
string-array.item: The split landscape player keeps a Home button without repeating the brand shown in the browsing pane.
Compact artwork and content-sized spacing bring playback controls and the following lyrics card higher, while preserving system insets and scrolling.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_14_bullets
string-array.item: The lyrics sheet includes Shuffle at the left of the playback controls, using the same shuffle state as the player.
Previous, play/pause and next have larger separate touch targets. The progress slider uses its own row in portrait and landscape.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_13_bullets
string-array.item: Advanced playback settings open in an independent scrollable window, above the bottom navigation and player.
The window accounts for system bars and the keyboard. Close it with the top arrow or Back; field autosave behavior is unchanged.

resources.string: Clear search account state and errors

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_12_bullets
string-array.item: Search rechecks the saved account when returning to the screen. It sends no queries while checking or without a connected account, retains the query, and respects Spotify cooldowns.
Errors distinguish authorization, permissions, request, server, connection, and incompatible responses. Cooldowns explain that signing in again is unnecessary.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_11_bullets
string-array.item: Cooldowns detected by the native client are saved even when an operation returns only an error without details. Startup restores the saved cooldown before enabling requests.
Saving is asynchronous: if the process stops before the write completes, the latest update may be lost.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_10_bullets
string-array.item: Normal Web API requests recheck the cooldown immediately before dispatch, including after waiting for a session or retrying an authentication error.
A rate-limit response starts the cooldown when its headers arrive, without waiting for its body. Session refresh also respects that pause. Manual diagnostic probes retain their exception.

resources.string: Hide songs and albums, a home button, and a bigger brand mark

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_9_bullets
string-array.item: A minus button next to every heart hides a song or an album forever: it disappears from every list and is skipped automatically if it starts playing. Restore hidden items from Settings > Hidden.
A home button next to the "Spoty by Darius" mark, present on every screen, closes the player and lyrics and returns straight to Home.
The "Spoty by Darius" mark is now twice as large.
The audio diagnostics report now filters system noise out of the logcat (Samsung floods it) and records every search failure with its exact cause.
Steering wheel, Bluetooth headset and Android Auto buttons (next, previous, play/pause) are now applied directly to playback, bypassing the default Media3 handling that dropped them on the car box.
When a search fails, the real Spotify error reaches the app instead of an unexplained empty result.

If Spotify rejects the account session (it happens when the app credentials change after signing in), Spoty drops that session and asks to connect the account again from Home, instead of failing silently in search, likes and lists.

The diagnostics report is shared as two files: summary (state, events, process exits) and logcat, so the summary fits whole in a message. It also records which lyrics provider answered and with what result.

resources.string: Spoty by Darius mark, car controls and steering wheel next button

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_8_bullets
string-array.item: Every screen now shows the "Spoty by Darius" brand mark in the top-right corner: home, search, library, album, artist, playlist and podcast details, the expanded player, landscape lyrics, and every settings screen.
The fullscreen landscape lyrics layout, the one used in the car, now has larger playback buttons and a shuffle button at the left edge.
The "next" button on the steering wheel, Bluetooth headsets and Android Auto now changes the song. The audio diagnostics report records the media keys received, to investigate play/pause and volume.

resources.string: Its own typeface controls for lyrics

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_7_bullets
string-array.item: The lyrics screen now has its own text controls in Appearance: an independent size, bold, and a choice of typeface (Sans, Serif, Monospace), separate from the general app font size. Lyrics can now be made larger and more legible, for example while driving.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_6_bullets
string-array.item: On some devices (depending on the manufacturer) playback failed on every track: the engine tried to write its temporary file to a system folder it was not allowed to, and retried over and over. Temporary files now go to the app\'s own folder, which is always writable.

resources.string: Controls no longer vanish without lyrics

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_5_bullets
string-array.item: On the lyrics screen, when a song had no synced lyrics the previous, play/pause and next buttons disappeared along with the progress bar. The controls now show whenever the displayed track is the one playing, with or without lyrics.

resources.string: Fewer requests to Spotify after a rate limit

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_4_bullets
string-array.item: While Spotify keeps a rate limit in place (HTTP 429), the native API client sends nothing and answers at once with how long is left. Only the diagnostics probe in Settings still reaches Spotify, to tell a real block from a window that already expired.
The access token is cached in memory and refreshed one refresh at a time, 60 seconds before it expires. A failed refresh is not repeated for two minutes.
Bottom-navigation tabs return to their existing screen instead of stacking a new copy on every tap. Each copy repeated the requests of that screen; they now run once.
Search history is no longer resolved against the network every time any setting changes: only new entries are looked up.
Podcast episode details, saved albums, shows and episodes, the device list and Android Auto browsing honour the rate-limit window and do not insist while it lasts.
Metadata lookups no longer retry a 429 on their own on top of the native retry, which already waits for the time Spotify indicates.
A second Spotify Connect initialisation no longer starts while another one is in flight.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_3_bullets
string-array.item: Custom Client ID and Client Secret entered in Settings were lost on app restart, silently falling back to the build-time credentials. They are now applied on every launch, and clearing them returns to the build-time ones, never to a third-party ID.

Removing a song from Liked Songs touched the episodes table and the song stayed marked. Every heart (player, detail, notification and Android Auto) now uses the same operation and ends up showing the same state.
Starting a radio and liking from the notification or the car did network work on the main thread. They run in the background, and the "done" notice appears only once the operation is confirmed.

In search, an earlier query finishing late overwrote the results of the newer one. Each search is bound to its text: only the results of what you typed last are shown, and clearing the field discards whatever was in flight. A network error is told apart from "no matches".

If a lyric was not found while the LRCLIB lookup was off, the app kept treating it as missing after you turned it on. Cache validity is now decided in one place, "not found" entries expire after six hours and a network error offers a retry.
Repeat and shuffle buttons on an external controller (Android Auto, headphones) did nothing even though they were advertised. They now work and show the same state as the in-app buttons.

"Play next" could change the current song, its position and the history. It now inserts the track ahead of the queue without touching what is playing, and reports when nothing was playing or the insert failed.

When an audio write was cut short or the output died (for example on Bluetooth loss), samples were lost with no recovery. Pending samples are now kept, the output is rebuilt with a bounded number of attempts and the diagnostics report shows the recovery counters.
Stored playlists show instantly and refresh in the background; if the network fails you keep what you had, with a notice to retry.
Home, Liked, playlists and search show clear waiting, error and retry notices, including Spotify rate limits with a countdown. A network error is no longer presented as "no content".

resources.string: The app respects Spotify rate limits

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_2_bullets
string-array.item: When Spotify answers "too many requests" (HTTP 429) the app reads how long to wait and stays away from the API until then. It used to retry immediately, making the block worse.
Liked sync no longer retries on a 429: it stops at once. Retries are reserved for real network drops.
There is one sync entry point: two screens asking at the same time share a single run, and it does not repeat within a minute (except the forced sync from Settings).
Settings → Accounts shows "Spotify is rate limiting requests. Try again in N s." with a countdown, and the connect button waits for it.
Fixed the cause of "Spoty is not responding": the profile lookup and several like actions did network work on the main thread. They now run in the background.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_1_bullets
string-array.item: The audio diagnostics report gains a "Process exits" section: the last ten times Android closed the app, with date, reason and, for a "Spoty is not responding" freeze, the main thread dump captured at that moment.
On startup the app logs one line with the reason for the previous exit, so it shows up in the next report.

string-array.name: changelog_1_7_0_bullets
string-array.item: The lyrics screen now has a heart at the top right, in portrait and in landscape. One tap adds the song to Liked Songs; another removes it.
The heart reflects the song you are looking at, even when it is not the one playing, and turns the accent color once the song is liked.

resources.string: LRCLIB lyrics when Spotify has none

string-array.name: changelog_1_6_0_bullets
string-array.item: When Spotify has no lyrics for a song, the app looks them up on lrclib.net by itself and shows them with a "Lyrics provided by LRCLIB" caption under the title. Synced lyrics follow the song as usual; plain text is shown static.
The lyrics screen no longer stays black: it says "Looking for the lyrics…" while searching and "We could not find the lyrics for this song" when no source has them.
New switch in Settings › Playback › Lyrics, "Look up lyrics on LRCLIB", on by default. Turning it off sends nothing to lrclib.net.
Found and missing lyrics are remembered per song, so the screen does not query again every time you open it.

resources.string: The lyrics sheet spans the full width

string-array.name: changelog_1_5_1_bullets
string-array.item: In landscape the lyrics sheet left the player visible at both sides. It now covers the whole screen.

string-array.name: changelog_1_5_0_bullets
string-array.item: New landscape view: the lyrics fill the whole screen with only three buttons at the bottom, previous, pause and next. It is the default whenever the phone or the car screen is in landscape.
The top-left arrow goes to the usual library (player on the left, list on the right), and the floating lyrics button returns to the fullscreen view.
Settings › Interface › Landscape view lets you pick between "Fullscreen lyrics" and "Player and content".

resources.string: One sign-in and cleaner lyrics in the car

string-array.name: changelog_1_4_0_bullets
string-array.item: A single "Connect Spotify account" button sets up playback and your library at once. There are no longer two sign-ins.
The app no longer asks for permissions at startup. Notifications and battery optimization are now two buttons under Settings › Permissions, and they show whether they are already granted.
Lyrics always open synced. The static mode moved to Settings › Playback › Lyrics as a switch.

On the lyrics screen the playback controls are smaller and sit in one row at the bottom, next to the progress bar. They no longer draw over the text, neither in the car nor with the phone in landscape.

string-array.name: changelog_1_3_2_bullets
string-array.item: New Settings › Audio diagnostics screen: builds a log with the device state, audio outputs, what the sound engine did and the system log, and shares it via WhatsApp, Telegram or email.
Two test tones that bypass Spotify, to tell whether the device lets the app\'s audio out at all.
The sound engine now records every relevant event: output creation, writes, errors, audio focus.

string-array.name: changelog_1_3_1_bullets
string-array.item: Spoty now requests Android audio focus at the moment playback starts, the way Spotify or YouTube do. iCarPlay-style boxes use that signal to open the audio channel to the head unit; without it the progress bar moved but nothing was heard.
If the device refuses to open the audio output, the app says so on screen instead of playing silently.
The permission prompts (notifications and battery) are now compact: a small icon, two lines and the buttons in one row.

string-array.name: changelog_1_3_0_bullets
string-array.item: Spoty shows up on the car screen with Android Auto.
Browse Recently played, Liked songs, Playlists and Top artists with real names and covers.
Open a playlist or an artist and tap a song to play it in that context.
Voice search: "Play [artist or song] on Spoty".
Because the app is not from Google Play, enable "Unknown sources" in Android Auto developer settings so it is listed.

string-array.name: changelog_1_2_0_bullets
string-array.item: The player now scrolls: swipe up and a card with the song lyrics appears.
The line being sung is highlighted and the card follows it on its own. Tap a line to jump to that moment.
The corner button opens the lyrics full screen.
The lead time and text size configured in Settings also apply to the card.

resources.string: The navigation bar no longer covers the player

string-array.name: changelog_1_1_3_bullets
string-array.item: With the classic navigation bar, the bar was drawn over the expanded player and hid the lyrics, queue and more row. It now hides while the player is open, just like the floating bar does.

resources.string: The lyrics button is visible again

string-array.name: changelog_1_1_2_bullets
string-array.item: The player cover now takes only the leftover space, so the lyrics, queue and more buttons never fall off the screen.
Those buttons are now shown in landscape too.

resources.string: Spoty in Spanish and lyrics settings

string-array.name: changelog_1_1_0_bullets
string-array.item: Rioplatense Spanish as the default language, with English as fallback.
System / Light / Dark theme mode in Appearance.
Lyrics lead-time slider so you can read each line before it is sung.
Lyrics text size slider.
This changelog screen.
New app icon.

resources.string: Spoty is an Android Spotify client built for Premium accounts. Play your music through librespot, control other devices with Spotify Connect, follow synced lyrics, add home-screen widgets, back up your settings and pick a theme that follows the album art or the system colors.

string-array.name: changelog_1_0_0_bullets
string-array.item: Playback through librespot for Spotify Premium accounts.
Spotify Connect device support.
Lyrics synced with playback.
Home-screen widgets.
Settings backup and restore.
Theme that follows the album art or the system colors.
